plan.chapterName: OpenStax Precalculus 2e, chapter 4: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
plan.contextChunk: This figure presents a single labeled sketch of a logistic growth curve on unscaled axes: a horizontal axis labeled t and a vertical axis labeled f(t), both double-arrowed and carrying no numeric ticks. A dashed orange horizontal line stretches across the upper part of the plot, tagged y = c at its left end and joined by a black leader to the annotation Carrying capacity. The solid dark blue curve enters from the lower left, crosses the vertical axis at a marked point labeled (0, c/(1 + a)) and identified as the Initial value of population, steepens through the middle of the frame, then flattens and runs rightward just beneath the dashed line without meeting it. A filled dot on the steepest part of the rise is labeled with the coordinates (ln(a)/b, c/2) and connected by a leader to the words Point of maximum growth. The curve's formula, f(t) = c/(1 + ae^(-bx)), is printed in blue to the right of the upper bend. The three annotations single out what the reader is meant to take from the shape: where the curve starts, where its slope is greatest, and the ceiling it approaches. Together they establish that growth of this kind accelerates only until the population reaches half the carrying capacity, after which the rate of increase falls away as the curve saturates.

Vertical axis labeled f(t), double-arrowed, no numeric ticks
Dashed orange horizontal asymptote line across the upper plot
Orange label 'y = c' at the left end of the dashed line
Black leader line from the dashed asymptote to the annotation 'Carrying capacity'
Solid dark blue S-shaped logistic curve entering from lower left, flattening toward the dashed line on the right
Blue formula label f(t) = c / (1 + ae^(-bt)) placed to the right of the upper bend
Marked point where the curve crosses the vertical axis, labeled (0, c/(1 + a))
Leader line from that y-intercept point to the annotation 'Initial value of population'
Filled blue dot on the steepest portion of the curve labeled (ln(a)/b, c/2)
Leader line from that dot to the annotation 'Point of maximum growth'
Faint horizontal guide line at height c/2 (revealed during exploration)
Draggable marker dot on the curve at the current t with its tangent line segment
Readout box showing current t, f(t), slope f'(t), and remaining gap c - f(t)
Vertical dropline from the marker to the t-axis
Optional bell-shaped growth-rate curve f'(t) shown in the derivative view
Legend distinguishing the population curve, the asymptote, and the growth-rate curve

interactions.label: Time t
interactions.teaches: Sliding the marker along the curve links position, steepness, and remaining room: the tangent is shallow at the start, steepest exactly at height c/2, and flattens again as the gap c - f(t) shrinks toward zero.

interactions.label: Growth rate b
interactions.teaches: b controls how abruptly the transition happens: larger b compresses the S into a sharp rise and pulls the maximum-growth point ln(a)/b toward the y-axis, while the ceiling c and the y-intercept c/(1+a) never move.

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: Overlaying the bell-shaped derivative shows that the inflection point of the S-curve is precisely the peak of the growth-rate curve, at f = c/2.

demo_steps.title: Where the population starts
demo_steps.narration: At t = 0 the curve crosses the vertical axis at c/(1 + a), a small fraction of the ceiling. The tangent here is nearly flat — with few individuals, growth is slow.

demo_steps.title: The ceiling: y = c
demo_steps.narration: The dashed orange line y = c is the carrying capacity. The blue curve rises toward it but never touches it — the gap c - f(t) keeps shrinking without reaching zero.

demo_steps.title: Fastest growth at half capacity
demo_steps.narration: Drag the marker to t = ln(a)/b and the tangent is at its steepest. Read the height: it is exactly c/2, half the carrying capacity — the point of maximum growth.

demo_steps.title: Slowing down past the halfway mark
demo_steps.narration: Past c/2 the population still increases, but the tangent flattens each step forward. Acceleration has turned into saturation.

demo_steps.title: The growth-rate curve
demo_steps.narration: Switching on f'(t) reveals a single hump whose peak sits directly under the inflection point. Growth rate rises, peaks at c/2, then decays — the S-curve is the accumulated story of that hump.

demo_steps.title: Turning b up: a sharper transition
demo_steps.narration: Increasing b steepens the rise and slides the maximum-growth point ln(a)/b leftward — the population reaches saturation sooner and more abruptly, but the ceiling c is unchanged.

demo_steps.title: Turning b down: a gentle climb
demo_steps.narration: With small b the S stretches out; the maximum-growth point moves far to the right and the curve takes much longer to approach the same carrying capacity.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Logistic growth is fastest not at the beginning and not near the ceiling, but exactly at half the carrying capacity — the inflection point (ln(a)/b, c/2) where the shrinking room to grow finally outweighs the growing population.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Unscaled first-quadrant-style sketch with double-arrowed black axes: t horizontal (arrow both ends), f(t) vertical, no numeric ticks. A dashed orange horizontal line spans the upper third, labeled 'y = c' in orange at its left end, with a thin black leader arrow from the line up-right to the text 'Carrying capacity'. The population curve is a thick dark navy-blue S: it enters flat from the lower left below the t-axis region, crosses the vertical axis at a small open/marked point labeled (0, c/(1+a)) in stacked-fraction math, rises steeply through mid-frame, then flattens and runs just beneath the dashed line to the right edge. A filled navy dot sits on the steepest part, labeled with the stacked coordinate pair (ln(a)/b, c/2) above-left and connected by a leader to 'Point of maximum growth' below-right. The formula f(t) = c/(1 + ae^(-bt)) appears in blue near the upper bend. Interactive additions: a bright marker dot on the curve with a straight tangent segment through it, a faint vertical dropline to the t-axis, a light gray horizontal guide at c/2, and a small readout panel (top-left or bottom-right) listing t, f(t), slope, and gap to c. In derivative view add a lighter teal/green bell curve for f'(t) drawn on the same frame with its peak vertically aligned to the inflection dot. Keep the hand-drawn textbook feel: no gridlines, generous white space, black serif-ish annotation text.

The dashed asymptote in the generated figure runs the full width with an arrowhead at the right end; the source's dashed line stops short of the axis arrow and has no arrowhead of its own.
